density.useAppInThread: Use app density in the OxeChat list

reduce.hint: Panels and lists change without animating; busy indicators turn slowly.

full.label: Full
full.hint: Short transitions on panels, lists and menus, even if the operating system asks for less.

summary.runToDetect: Run Health check to detect installed CLIs
summary.installThenRun: Install a CLI, then run Health check

onboarding.body: OXESpace launches agents as local CLIs. Install one of the guides below, ensure the command is on PATH, then run Health check.

empty.hint: Run a health check to discover installed agent CLIs.

card.notOnPath: Not on PATH — install or Fix path

newAccess.title: New conversations
newAccess.label: Access a new conversation starts with
newAccess.perConversation: You can change it in each conversation, from its access chip.

hint.read-only: The agent reads the project and changes nothing.
hint.workspace-write: The agent edits files in the project and asks before it runs a command.
hint.full-access: The agent runs commands and edits files without asking.

idle.title: Idle conversations
idle.hint: Each open OxeChat conversation keeps an agent process and its MCP servers running. Closing idle ones frees memory; your next message resumes the same session. A conversation with a running turn, a question, queued messages, a background task or a permission allowed for the session stays open.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.description: Set the default font, cursor and behavior for every workspace. Workspace overrides remain independent.
terminal.sizeHint: Ctrl + / Ctrl − / Ctrl 0 in a terminal
terminal.blinkHint: Animate the caret in focused terminals
terminal.resumeHint: After OXESpace restarts, Claude Code and Codex panes reopen the session they were in
terminal.agentsFullAccessOn: Agents started in a terminal now skip their permission prompts
terminal.agentsFullAccessHint: Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity started by OXESpace in a terminal run commands and edit files without asking. Off: each agent asks the way its own CLI does. A command that already chooses its mode keeps it.
terminal.resumeBypass: Resume sessions that skipped permission prompts the same way
terminal.resumeBypassOn: Resumed sessions now skip permission prompts when they did before
terminal.resumeBypassHint: A Claude Code session started with its permission prompts skipped resumes the same way after a restart or Restore session. Off: it resumes asking for permission.

hooks.title: Agent status hooks
hooks.callout: Let Claude Code and Codex report working / waiting / done themselves instead of guessing from terminal output. Writes to the agent's own config; your existing hooks are kept.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Choose when OXESpace gets your attention.
notifications.notify: Notify when an agent needs you
notifications.notifyHint: Desktop alerts when a background agent finishes, exits, or errors. Clicking focuses the terminal.
notifications.onlyUnwatched: Only for terminals you are not watching.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: Keep OXESpace and its tools up to date.

status.availableManual: Update {{version}} available — install it from Releases
status.availableAuto: Update {{version}} available — downloading in the background

updates.checkTitle: Check GitHub Releases for a new version

hint.manual: Development and Linux package installs cannot update in place. Use the latest release or update your development checkout.
hint.ask: Downloaded updates install when you restart.
hint.auto: Downloads in the background. Restart to apply.

preferences.label: How OXESpace updates
preferences.stayHint: Keep this version until you turn this off.
preferences.betaOn: You get each beta as it comes out. Turning this off keeps your version until a newer stable one is out.
preferences.betaOff: Try upcoming features early. Betas are tested, but can change before the stable release.

hint.pinned: Staying on v{{version}}: OXESpace does not check or download updates. Check for updates still tells you what is new.
hint.auto: Checks every few hours, downloads in the background and installs when you restart.
hint.notify: Checks every few hours and tells you when a version is out. Nothing downloads until you choose.
hint.off: Never checks on its own. Use Check for updates when you want to know.

policy.title: Policy
policy.intro: Rules that block what agents may use: providers, tools, MCP servers, skills, databases and shared memory. They only block; they never grant anything. To change a rule, edit the file. The last matching rule decides, so the managed file wins.

user.label: User
user.hint: Applies to you on this computer

managed.label: Managed
managed.hint: Installed by an administrator; has the final word

policy.fileError: This file has an error and is ignored.

activity.title: Agent activity
activity.hint: What agents changed through OXESpace, and what you decided.
activity.sourcesFailed: Some sources couldn't be read. The rest is up to date.
activity.changeGone: This change isn't in the working tree any more: it was committed, undone or moved.
activity.containerGone: This container was removed. Only its name and start time are kept.

keyboard.title: Keyboard
keyboard.intro: Shortcuts work in the view named by each group. Press ? outside a text field to see the ones for the current screen. A focused terminal keeps every key except the command palette, Settings and the sidebar shortcuts.
keyboard.taken: {{chord}} is already the shortcut for {{bindings}}. Press another one, or change that shortcut first.
keyboard.capturing: Press the new shortcut, or Esc to cancel

agentConfig.commandChanged: {{name}} now starts with the new command
agentConfig.deleteDescription: “{{name}}” is removed from OXESpace. Terminals already running it keep running.
agentConfig.customDescription: A skill prompt that runs on top of a built-in agent.
agentConfig.description: The name and command OXESpace uses to start this agent.
agentConfig.name: Name
agentConfig.promptPlaceholder: You are a Java 8+ expert. Review this code for best practices, performance, and correctness.

devices.title: Phone and devices
devices.intro: Use OXESpace from your Android phone on the same network: follow conversations, answer requests and watch terminals. The phone talks only to this computer, over your local network, never through the internet.
devices.loadFailed: Could not read the phone connection.
devices.unavailable: The phone connection is not available in this version.

gateway.title: Phone connection
gateway.label: Let phones on this network connect
gateway.hint: Off by default. When on, OXESpace listens only on private network addresses, over an encrypted connection that only paired phones can use.
gateway.failed: Could not change the phone connection: {{error}}
gateway.on: Phones can now connect to this computer

network.publicTitle: Windows calls “{{network}}” a Public network, so phones can’t reach this computer
network.publicBody: Mark this Wi-Fi as Private in Windows Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi › this network › Network profile type. Or allow OXESpace on public networks in Windows Defender Firewall › Allow an app through the firewall. Only do that on a network you trust.

firewall.title: Before phones can connect
firewall.windowsAsk: Windows will ask whether OXESpace may accept connections. Allow it on private networks, such as your home or office Wi-Fi.
firewall.windowsPublic: If Windows calls your Wi-Fi a Public network, it blocks phones even when you allow OXESpace on private networks. Mark your home or office Wi-Fi as Private, or allow OXESpace on public networks too.
firewall.otherAsk: Your system may ask whether OXESpace may accept incoming connections. Allow it so phones on your network can reach this computer.
firewall.internet: Nothing is exposed to the internet. OXESpace listens only on private network addresses, and only phones you pair here can use the connection.
firewall.later: If you refuse, phones cannot reach this computer. You can change the answer later in the firewall settings of your system.

blocked.title: A firewall rule blocks OXESpace
blocked.text: A Block rule in Windows Defender Firewall stops phones from reaching this computer, and it wins over any Allow rule. OXESpace never removes it: ask your IT, or remove it in Windows Defender Firewall.

public.title: This network is Public, so Windows blocks phones
public.text: Windows keeps devices out on Public networks. If this is your home or office Wi-Fi, set it to Private: Windows Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi › this network › Private network. OXESpace doesn't change it for you.

noRule.title: Windows Firewall doesn't let phones in yet
noRule.text: No firewall rule lets OXESpace accept connections from phones on this network.

firewallCheck.noInspection: OXESpace couldn't read the firewall settings, so this is a guess. Allowing it is still safe.
firewallCheck.uac: Windows will ask for permission. Nothing changes if you say No.

repair.explain: OXESpace adds one Windows Firewall rule, "{{name}}": {{rule}}. You can remove it here later.
repair.done: Verified: phones can now reach this computer on private networks
repair.notVerified: The rule could not be verified. Check again, or add it in Windows Defender Firewall.

undo.explain: OXESpace removes only the rule it added, "{{name}}" ({{rule}}). Phones won't reach this computer until it is allowed again.
undo.done: Verified: the firewall rule is removed
undo.notVerified: The removal could not be verified. Check again.

name.title: Name of this computer
name.label: Name phones see
name.hint: Shown on the phone when it connects. The network name of your computer is never sent.
name.empty: Type a name, or use the default.

pairing.title: Pair a phone
pairing.hint: Open OXESpace on the phone and scan the code. Each code works once and lasts two minutes.
pairing.needsGateway: Turn on the phone connection first.
pairing.full: You have reached {{max}} phones. Remove one to pair another.
pairing.qrLabel: Pairing QR code. Point the phone's camera at the code.
pairing.fingerprintHint: The phone checks this before it trusts the connection.
pairing.failed: Could not show a pairing code: {{error}}
pairing.unreadable: The pairing code could not be read. Show a new code.

prompt.title: Pair {{device}}?
prompt.description: Pair only if the phone shows the same code.

list.title: Paired phones
list.emptyHint: Pair a phone above to see it here.
list.removeDescription: The phone is disconnected right away and can no longer connect. To use it again, pair it again.

typing.title: Typing in terminals
typing.none: Phones cannot type in any terminal. To allow it in one terminal, open its ⋯ menu and choose "Allow typing from the phone". It turns off again when OXESpace restarts.
typing.some: Terminals a phone can type in: {{count}}. It turns off again when OXESpace restarts.
typing.stopAll: Stop typing from the phone everywhere
typing.failed: Could not stop typing from the phone: {{error}}

scope.title: What a phone can do
scope.deskOnly: Requests that only this computer can answer (guarded actions, permissions and secret questions) stay here.

skillsList.title: Skills
skillsList.intro: Markdown prompts in ~/.oxe/skills and the project's .oxe/skills. The project's wins on a shared name. Run one with /.
skillsList.emptyBody: Add a Markdown file to .oxe/skills in the project.

tools.title: Tools
tools.intro: The groups of OXESpace MCP tools that agents in this project are offered, how each group is offered and what it costs. Agents that start after a change get it. Modes are saved in the project's file:
tools.loadFailed: Could not read the tool groups
tools.unavailable: This version of OXESpace cannot show this yet.

providers.title: How each provider gets the tools
providers.claude: Groups always on send their definitions with every request. Groups on demand send only the tool names, and Claude loads a definition when it searches for it.
providers.codex: Every group that is not off is available from the start; there is no turning a group on during a session. Codex sends no definitions up front and loads them as it needs them.

totals.title: What a Claude conversation sends with every request
totals.plain: A conversation that asks for nothing extra

sections.roleIntro: These come with what a conversation or terminal is: a team member, a delegated task, or an agent in an OxeCode terminal. They cannot be changed here.

core.name: Core tools
core.description: Source code, search and memory lookups, in every conversation.

orchestration.name: Orchestration
orchestration.description: Start other agents and conversations, delegate tasks and follow Agent Work.

data.name: Data
data.description: Databases and containers; every data read and change is approved by you in OxeQuery.

app.name: App
app.description: Git, GitHub, conversations, skills, MCP servers, search and usage. Pushes, pull requests and releases are approved by you.

team.name: Team
team.description: Messages and status between members of an agent team.

worker.name: Delegated task
worker.description: A conversation that runs a delegated task or an Agent Work task: context, updates, checkpoints and the result.

code.name: OxeCode terminal
code.description: Agents in OxeCode terminals: panes, terminals, scripts, background jobs, worktrees, tasks and agents. Always on there, never offered to an OxeChat conversation.

modeHints.always: Every definition goes with each request.
modeHints.on-demand: Only the tool names go with each request; an agent loads a tool when it needs it.
modeHints.off: Not offered in this project, and a session cannot turn it on.

tools.modeLabel: How {{group}} is offered in this project

sourceHint.default: The project's oxe.yaml does not set this group.
sourceHint.role: Follows what the conversation or terminal is.

rules.intro: Each group also lists its tools: run without asking, ask you (the default), or block. Blocking holds everywhere; running without asking holds in OxeChat conversations.
rules.label: Rule for {{tool}}

scope.everywhere: Blocked everywhere: OxeChat conversations, OxeCode terminals and MCP.
scope.oxechat: Runs without asking in OxeChat conversations; agents in OxeCode terminals follow their own CLI's permissions.

source.user: Set in your user policy; change it there.
source.managed: Set by your organization; it cannot be changed here.
source.reads: A read-only lookup, allowed by "Approve read-only commands automatically" in a conversation's Permissions. Turn that off to be asked.

rules.confirmLevel: Always asks: this tool can do things you confirm each time.
rules.loadFailed: Could not read the tool rules
rules.otherEmpty: No rules for other MCP servers' tools in this project.

confirmAllow.title: Run {{tool}} without asking?
confirmAllow.description: In this project's OxeChat conversations, {{tool}} will run without asking you first. Agents in OxeCode terminals keep following their own CLI's permissions. You can change it back here at any time.

policy.title: User and organization policy
policy.intro: Rules about tools and MCP servers from your user and managed policy files. Read only: they are changed in the files (Application › Policy shows where).
policy.empty: No user or organization rule about tools or MCP servers.

invalidYaml.title: {{file}} can't be read
invalidYaml.body: The file has an error, so the modes below can't be changed here. Agents keep the tools they had before the error. Fix the file by hand and choose Reload.
invalidYaml.bodyLastValid: The file has an error. Agents keep using the last modes that could be read, shown below. To change them, fix the file by hand and choose Reload.
invalidYaml.bodyDefaults: The file has an error and has never been read, so agents use the app's defaults, shown below. To change them, fix the file by hand and choose Reload.

noProject.title: No project folder open
noProject.body: Open a workspace or project folder to configure project MCP tool groups and oxe.yaml rules.

data.title: Data
data.description: What OXESpace keeps on this computer, and for how long.
data.exportDesc: Data from features removed in 1.5, in one JSON file.
data.nothingToExport: Nothing to export: this profile has no data from the features removed in 1.5.

agentPermissions.title: What agents can do
agentPermissions.description: Everything agents may do without asking. Revoke anything here.

alwaysOn.denyAndHold: Deny is the default, and irreversible approvals need a hold.

hostsProxy.toggleLabel: Log the hosts agents connect to
hostsProxy.toggleHint: Logs hosts for programs that use HTTP_PROXY. Never paths, headers or bodies.
hostsProxy.turnedOnNotice: Applies to new agents' programs that use HTTP_PROXY. Some, like ssh or Node's fetch, skip it.
hostsProxy.turnedOffNotice: Logging stopped. Agents already running keep working until they end.

clearDialog.title: Clear outgoing connections?
clearDialog.body: Clear the recorded hosts? This can't be undone.

usage.toggleHint: Counted on this computer only. Nothing is sent.

clearDialog.title: Clear usage?
clearDialog.body: Clear the usage count? This can't be undone.
